theBigPicture: Middle East tensions flared overnight as drone attacks hit airports in Saudi Arabia and an oil tanker, pushing crude oil to war-premium levels near $125 a barrel. Russia carried out one of its deadliest strikes on Ukrainian civilians in months, killing 22 people as they slept, while analysts warn Moscow is deliberately testing whether Europe will stop pushing back. Financial markets are otherwise calm, but the fuel price squeeze is the story most likely to hit your wallet first.

householdImpact.energyAndFuel: Oil is trading near $125 a barrel because of Middle East fighting, and that typically shows up at the gas pump within a few weeks. Home heating bills should stay steady for now since natural gas prices are normal, but a hurricane threat in the US could add extra bumps to fuel costs.
householdImpact.borrowingAndMortgages: Financial markets are unusually calm right now, which helps keep mortgage and auto loan rates steady. The main risk is that expensive oil reignites inflation, which could keep credit card and borrowing costs higher for longer.
householdImpact.groceriesAndSupplyChain: Attacks on ships and rising fuel costs make it more expensive to move food around the world, and those costs eventually land at the grocery checkout. Expect gradual price creep on imported goods and anything hauled long distances by truck.
householdImpact.jobsAndSavings: Stock markets are steady and financial conditions are easy, so retirement accounts are not in danger mode today. The big wildcard is a wider Middle East conflict, which could rattle markets and slow hiring if oil keeps climbing.

globalFlashpoints.summary: A Russian missile destroyed part of an apartment block while families slept, killing 22 people including five children, and attacks have caused power outages across four regions.
Houthi attacks struck airports in Riyadh and Abha, killing three people, and an attack on an oil tanker pushed crude prices sharply higher.
No major flashpoints today, though public anger in Japan over a US Marine's arrest in a woman's killing is straining an important alliance.

Nationwide protests in India over voter list changes, continuing French high school demonstrations, and US campus protests are keeping streets active, though nothing has yet disrupted daily life at large scale.

topStories.headline: Oil Jumps as Attacks Hit Saudi Airports and a Tanker
topStories.whyItMatters: Attacks that kill civilians at airports and strike oil shipping raise the odds of a wider regional war. That is a direct driver of what you will pay at the gas pump in the coming weeks.

topStories.headline: Russian Strike Kills 22, Including Five Children, as Ukraine's Power Grid Takes More Hits
topStories.whyItMatters: The war is hitting civilians hardest just as cold weather arrives, and attacks are knocking out electricity for whole regions. Europe's energy prices and defense spending trace directly back to this conflict.

topStories.headline: France Invites Britain to 'Come All the Way Back' to the EU
topStories.whyItMatters: A warmer UK-EU relationship could smooth trade rules and affect prices on everyday imported goods. The British Prime Minister heads to Berlin this week to discuss closer security cooperation against Russia.

topStories.headline: Israel Sharply Cuts Britain's Diplomatic Presence in Jerusalem
topStories.whyItMatters: The move is retaliation for UK sanctions over West Bank settlements and shows cracks forming between longtime allies. Diplomatic rifts like this can eventually affect trade, travel, and consular services for citizens abroad.

topStories.headline: The Boss's AI Is Listening: Co-op Rates Every Customer Phone Call
topStories.whyItMatters: A major employer is using automated technology to score workers' calls, which critics call oppressive and dystopian. It is a preview of how AI monitoring could spread to many more workplaces.

whatWeAreWatching: Whether oil keeps climbing — watch for further attacks on tankers and any disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most important oil shipping lane.
The British Prime Minister's first official visit to Germany, where security cooperation against Russia will be the headline topic.
France's Prime Minister has promised a plan to fix the education system by the end of the month — if students reject it again, expect more street protests.
A US hurricane threat compounding pressure on fuel prices heading into the weekend.
Ukraine's power grid resilience as winter approaches, after attacks caused outages in four regions.
